- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.3) in recent days, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3) and price is rising, cap forecast growth to prevent overshoot.  
- After a sharp spike in price, reduce forecast momentum for next 3–5 days to allow mean reversion.  
- If true outcome shows early sharp drop after a peak, model should adjust downward by 5–10% in next forecast.  
- When sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.2) and price is trending, forecast should not exceed 1.5x recent high unless confirmed by 2+ consecutive positive sentiment.  
- If forecast is consistently above true outcome by >10% for 3+ consecutive days, reduce forecast by 5–10% and re-evaluate sentiment alignment.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >15% from forecast in first 5 days, reset forecast to mean of last 7–10 days + sentiment-adjusted drift.
